constraints.service_description: Half the outlets in the apartment lost power

success_criteria.notes: Success if the assistant schedules an emergency electrical visit at the earliest window available in the tool results and reports the provider, window, and confirmation code.

task.objective: Half my outlets just died, can someone come today

injected_behaviors.instructions: The user is anxious about the outage and repeatedly presses for speed — asking 'how soon can they get here?' and 'is that the fastest option?' after each assistant message. They accept the earliest available slot rather than comparing options, and push back briefly if the assistant suggests a later time.

persona.name: Kevin O'Brien
persona.bio: Kevin O'Brien works for a Boston think tank analyzing fiscal and monetary policy. He writes reports on tax policy, labor markets, and economic growth strategies, and his work gets cited by congressional staffers and journalists. He has strong opinions about which economic theories actually work in practice.
sample_messages: Working on the labor market report - need the latest BLS data pulled and formatted for the appendix
Panel discussion at brookings next month, need train tickets to DC and hotel for 2 nights
Can you track down that CBO report from 2019 on supply-side reforms? Need it for the lit review

messages.output_raw: Half the outlets in my apartment just lost power, need an electrician today if at all possible. How soon can someone get here?

</think>
<plan>

<action type="say">
I can check who can come today and how soon, but I need a couple details.

1) What’s the service address (city + ZIP at minimum)?
2) Is anything unsafe right now—smell of burning, sparks, hot outlets, or tripped breakers that won’t reset?
3) How urgent is this for you: absolutely ASAP (emergency) or later today is fine (same-day)?
4) Any preferred time window today (morning, afternoon, evening)?

If you do smell burning, see scorch marks, or feel hot outlets, turn off the breaker to that circuit (or the main if you’re unsure) and avoid using those outlets until an electrician arrives.</action>
